claims.text: A molybdenum-based alloy interlayer can bridge the thermal mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
A molybdenum-based alloy interlayer can bridge the chemical mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed interlayer enhances W/CuCrZr joint integrity under nuclear fusion reactor conditions.
Directly interfaced W and CuCrZr typically develop high interfacial stresses because their coefficients of thermal expansion are mismatched.
Directly interfaced W and CuCrZr have poor chemical compatibility.
Selected alloying additions can give a molybdenum-based interlayer a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
The proposed molybdenum-based alloy can act as a diffusion barrier between W and CuCrZr.
The interlayer creates a smooth transition in thermal-expansion properties between W and CuCrZr.
The interlayer supports strong metallurgical bonds with both W and CuCrZr.
An intermediate thermal-expansion response reduces interfacial stress during thermal cycling.
The interlayer's metallurgical compatibility and diffusion-barrier properties mitigate detrimental interdiffusion during thermal cycling.
The proposed interlayer improves the mechanical integrity of the W/CuCrZr joint.
The proposed interlayer reduces interfacial cracking under extreme thermal and irradiation conditions.
The proposed interlayer improves load transfer across the W/CuCrZr joint.
Direct W-to-CuCrZr bonding typically suffers delamination or cracking because of thermal-expansion discrepancies and chemical-interaction issues.
Interlayer effectiveness depends on maintaining a precise composition that provides suitable thermal expansion and bonding.
Interlayer performance may degrade when temperature or irradiation exceeds its design limits.
